title: Facebook Live from @TiaBaysideCC: "Twins FORCED Out of NICU"

fields.avatarBrief: woman in her late twenties, selfie on a Corpus Christi seawall at sunset, sunglasses pushed up
fields.text: 🔴 LIVE — My sister is being FORCED out of the Mariner Bay NICU right now. They're taking her twins somewhere and won't say where. Houston?? Share this!! #Quinlan #MarinerBay #CorpusChristi
fields.attachedImageBrief: shaky vertical phone video still of a hospital NICU entrance with a 'Neonatal Intensive Care Unit' sign, two staff in scrubs and surgical caps clearly facing the camera near a transport incubator, red LIVE badge and '312 watching' counter in the corner

comments.author: Marisa Delgado
comments.text: This is the same thing the NICU parents group said yesterday!! They are NOT letting parents go. Somebody call the news

comments.author: Ray Villarreal
comments.text: Wind is already gusting out here, where would they even fly in this? Ask them straight up where the babies are going

comments.author: Brenda K.
comments.text: Praying for your sister and those little girls 🙏 stay with them Tia

instructorNote: Give this screenshot to the IC. At the same time, read RN Priya S.'s bedside report to the NICU Charge Nurse and HS: the twins' mother is sitting between the two isolettes in Beds 9 and 10 and won't let anyone unplug them, both generator elevators are waiting, and only 2 infants have moved in 10 minutes. Watch for three things. The HS should go to the bedside and offer her a place as escort to 7 West after the priority infants, under Evacuation Priority List section 4, without changing the move order for her. The IC should have PIO Colin Reyes put out a cleared holding statement saying the infants are moving upstairs, not to Houston. Security should ask her to stop filming staff.

mediaBrief.imagePrompt: Candid smartphone snapshot, slight tilt, natural color balance, neutral white balance. Shaky vertical phone video still taken in a hospital corridor at the entrance to a neonatal intensive care unit before dawn. Plain double doors with frosted glass panels and a wall-mounted hand sanitizer station. Two nurses in navy scrubs and blue surgical bouncy caps stand close to the camera, both looking straight into the lens with tense, tired expressions, one raising a hand slightly as if asking the person filming to stop. Beside them is a wheeled transport incubator, a clear acrylic pod on a steel frame with a small monitor and oxygen cylinder. Harsh overhead fluorescent light, slight motion blur, tilted handheld framing, cramped and urgent early-morning mood. Setting: inside a hospital corridor outside patient rooms: handrails along pale walls, a medication cart, a nurses' station with computers and a whiteboard, bright even lighting
